hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Three layers, each depending only on the one below. Layer 1, the file commit: the store has one write operation for a file, which in a single LMDB transaction replaces the file's entities, replaces its relationships and its pending relationships, and advances the repository's generation and completeness counters. It grows out of the existing whole-file replacement (reindexFile), which already replaces a file's entities in one transaction but removes relationships only for entities that disappeared from the file; the commit goes further and replaces the outgoing relationships of every entity of the file. The indexer's refresh, the delete event and the repair all call it; a file is selected for it by one filter built from the repository's ignore files. A relationship is never dropped in the commit: when its target is not stored it becomes a pending row, and pending rows are completed only by the passes that own them: the cross-file pass for code symbols, and the two endpoint passes of the external-services Epic for theirs. Layer 2, the recorded state: one row per repository holds the generation and what is known to be incomplete (relationships awaiting a target that is in an indexed repository, relationships that could not be written, entities without vectors). The four repository status values keep their meaning; completeness is a separate field read from this row and shown wherever status is shown, so a repository with anything outstanding does not read as fully ready. Layer 3, derived data: evidence is a one-byte value on the relationship row, written in the commit, by the cross-file pass and by every other writer of a stored relationship; subsystem grouping, subsystem summaries and model-proposed document relationships are queued passes that start only from a repository whose state is complete, write their own tables, and stamp what they wrote with the generation it was computed from. All new stored data arrives as steps on the existing migration chain (SCHEMA_VERSION 4 onward); no existing edge key or kind byte changes.

consumedContracts.name: IndexState
consumedContracts.purpose: The recorded per-repository state: the generation of the graph and what is known to be incomplete. Written in the same transaction as every file commit and by the cross-file pass; read by repository status, by the commit's callers, and by every derived pass to decide whether it may run and whether what it wrote is stale.

consumedContracts.name: FileCommit
consumedContracts.purpose: The one write operation for a file's rows. Everything that adds, replaces or removes a file's entities and relationships hands the store one of these and gets one transaction. The commit removes the outgoing relationships of every entity of the file before writing the new set, leaves the incoming relationships of surviving entities in place, and returns to pending any incoming relationship whose target entity it removes. Entities that are not of the file (shared module stubs) are ensured to exist under the shared-modules rows and are otherwise untouched.

consumedContracts.name: RelationEvidence
consumedContracts.purpose: How a relationship was established, stored as the value of its row and returned wherever relationships are read. An empty value, which is what every existing row holds, reads as 'unknown', so no existing row is rewritten.

boundary.internal: The reading of links and references between documents, and from a document to code, as relationships of the existing REFERENCES kind written in the file commit with evidence 'extracted'; the queued mid-tier pass over new or changed documents and its own table of model-proposed relationships; the hand-checked set, the measurement, and the recorded figures that switch the capability on or leave it off; the merging of model-proposed relationships into reads with evidence 'model'; the status line when no CLI provider is available.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The rule that a relationship with an absent target becomes pending instead of being skipped, at each of the six places in src/db/relations.ts where one is lost today (the resolved write's skip on a missing endpoint and its skip on a kind with no byte, promoteToResolved, promoteResolvedBatch, and the pending write's discard of a row without its file or repository and of a row whose repository is not registered), each either kept as pending or counted as unwritable with a reason; the set of files whose parse or commit failed in a full index, persisted with their paths until they next commit; which fields of the state are recounted on open and which are persisted and carried over; the classification of a pending relationship as awaiting-target, ambiguous or no-candidate, with the external-service rows classed apart and the two endpoint passes counted in when a full index is finished; the class is stored on the pending row itself, in its existing free-form record, so no stored form changes, a row the cross-file pass has not yet attempted counts as awaiting-target, and the recount on open reads the stored class and does not run resolution again; the extension of the cross-file pass to complete relationships awaiting a target by id, for imports and the other code-symbol kinds as well as calls and inheritance, and to follow a re-exporting file to the function it re-exports; the lookup of pending rows by the id they await, with its migration step, and the pass after a file event visiting the rows that await an entity of the files just committed; the change of the reindex request so that it deletes the repository's rows in the graph store and the vector store and builds them again from every file, in place of today's skip of unchanged files, with no separate repair request, returning to pending the relationships that other repositories hold into the deleted entities, and its queuing by the migration for every repository indexed before this change, which starts as not complete; the storing of the repository entity so that the manifest step's dependency relationships are written; the measurement on this repository, before and after a repair, of the awaiting-target, ambiguous, no-candidate and unwritable counts, with unwritable expected to be zero; the IndexState row, its migration step, its recount on open, and the derivation of repository status from it, as a completeness field returned beside the unchanged status by the daemon's status and stats requests and shown in the CLI's repository pane and in both editor plugins; and the analyzer's read of it: an analyzer lookup that reads relationships of a repository that is not complete says so in its result, with the counts, so that an answer over an incomplete graph is not returned as a plain fact. The choice, in this Story's design, of the function reached only through a re-exporting file that the repair is measured on, since the issue's own example (pickScope) has been removed from the source. Raising the log level of a refused relationship from debug is internal. Until Story s2 lands, s1 applies its rule inside the existing separate writes.

The extension of the existing whole-file replacement into the file commit (relationships and pending rows in the same transaction as entities; outgoing relationships of surviving entities replaced, not only those of entities that disappeared; incoming relationships of a removed entity returned to pending), the move of the indexer's refresh and delete paths and of the clean-up pass's removal of a stored file onto it, and the retirement of the separate delete-then-upsert sequence in the indexer. The handling of vectors after the commit: writing the entity row with its embedding marker empty and setting it in a second transaction only after the vector write succeeds, counting an entity with an empty marker in IndexState, comparing entity ids with the vector table on open in both directions, so that a vector left behind by a failed removal is deleted before a plain insert can meet it, and the extension of the existing reembed job to run on daemon start and after an index, with a vector write for an entity whose marker is empty made an upsert, except for an entity first allocated in the same commit, which keeps the plain insert. Three things in that job change with it: it applies the embed step's own selection instead of forcing every entity, so empty-body entities (external endpoints, module stubs) stay unselected and uncounted; its update of an embedding writes the vector first and sets the marker in a second transaction, where today it sets the marker first; and the marker carries the model of the backend that is active, not one fixed name. Which entities count as unembedded (those the embed step selects) and the separate recorded reason when the embedding backend is unavailable. The count of a file whose commit fails on a file event. The queue rule that index jobs go ahead of other jobs and that a long job yields between its units, so that a commit is not held behind a model pass. How a reader sees the old or the new set during a commit is the store's ordinary transaction isolation and needs no new mechanism.

The by-file and by-repository index of entity rows, its migration step that builds it for an existing store, and its upkeep. No single entity-row write exists today: there are seven raw put and remove sites across src/db/entities.ts and src/db/graph/migrations.ts, and the existing name index is kept in step by a helper each site must remember to call. This Story introduces one put and one remove function for entity rows that maintain the name index and the new index together, routes every raw site through them, and adds a test that fails when a raw put or remove appears outside them. Upkeep therefore sits beneath every caller, so that neither today's writers nor the file commit need to know of it and this Story does not depend on s2. The two reads (findEntitiesByFile, listEntitiesForRepo) keep their results and their callers; a new existence check answers whether a repository holds any entity, and the analyzer's scope check uses it.

The cause, which ISSUE-0d577569 records as not known, was reproduced on 2026-10-11 and is not the system's semaphore limit, which the library's message names, but the loss of the daemon's own file lock on the store's lock file, after which another process that opens and closes the store removes the store's semaphores; the daemon's next write then fails with the library's message about the limit, and its exit hangs in the library's close. What in the daemon closes a second descriptor on the lock file is not yet identified. First, therefore, the remedy that does not depend on finding it: the live store is opened by the daemon alone, and any other process is refused it. Second, a bound on the whole shutdown including the store's close, so that a close that hangs ends in an exit. Third, recording a store failure of this kind and stating it in the daemon's status. None of this is consumed by another Story.

The refusal, with a named error and its own code, of a search or analyze request about a repository whose status is indexing, at the analyzer's scope check and at the daemon's search requests, carrying the status and how far the run has got (files done of files selected, and when it began), read from the indexer's running job; the tools that rest on the analyzer (the workflow steps, triage, code review) pass that error on as it is. The order of the analyzer's run: the refusal of a scope the index does not hold comes before a size is announced, or the announcement says the size could not be counted. The named cause and error code for a failed read of the last-indexed time and for a failed lookup, and the three other defects of ISSUE-e2bcadd9 (the wrong provider named, the scope resolved before the cache, and failure text matched inside echoed output). This Story does not read IndexState: it works with the checks the analyzer has today, so that it stays independent of s1.

The in-process matcher of the gitignore grammar over nested ignore files and its conformance test against git; the move onto the one filter of every site that reads the list today in src/indexer/index.ts (the full walk, the start-up scan for changed files, the file event, the clean-up pass, and the two places that seed the list when a repository is registered), of the watcher, and of the analyzer's reader, its two exploration walkers and its infra walker (src/analyze/runtimes/infra/_shared.ts), each of which has its own list of names today, and of the indexer's source-root detection (src/indexer/source-roots.ts), whose own list would otherwise hide a package in a directory the filter includes; a search of the source for such lists found five more, in the daemon's four file-search tools (glob, grep, list-dir, recent under src/daemon/tools/builtins/search) and in the review probe (src/workflow/review/probe.ts), which search the working tree as text, do not decide what the index holds, and are deliberately left as they are; the filter keeps answering for a directory that holds an included file, as the analyzer's reader does now; the retirement of the bare-name list and of the ignore entry in the repository's .insrc config; the two built-in exclusions (generated or minified files, the .insrc directory) applied inside the filter so that the full walk and the file event no longer differ on them; the handling of a change to an ignore file as an event that removes and adds files, and the comparison by content hash of the clone's exclude file and the global ignore file, which the watcher cannot see, whenever the filter is used; the queued step that proposes a root ignore file with the cheap-tier model when a repository is added without one, its fallback, and the rule that an existing file is never written. Two points were decided by the stakeholder: the filter honours all three of git's ignore sources (the .gitignore files, the clone's exclude file, the user's global ignore file), and a file git tracks is indexed even when a rule matches it, so the filter takes git's list of tracked files as an input and a plain folder is filtered by the rules alone.

The one-byte encoding of evidence as the value of a relationship row; the points in the per-file resolver and the cross-file pass that decide 'extracted' or 'inferred' ('chosen' is reserved and not written, since an ambiguous relationship stays pending with its candidates); the passing of evidence as an argument to the store's resolved write and promote operations, so that the two endpoint passes write 'inferred' and the manifest step writes 'extracted' and no relationship written after this change reads 'unknown'; the carrying of evidence through the store's traversal reads and the daemon's caller and callee requests; the marking of inferred and chosen relationships in the analyzer's lookups and answers. No migration rewrites existing rows, since an empty value reads as 'unknown'.

The grouping of a complete repository's code entities into subsystems, its determinism, the tables for membership, connections and summaries and their migration step; the queued pass and its trigger on a new generation; the cheap-tier summary of a subsystem whose membership changed; the daemon request that returns subsystems; the addition of subsystem context to the analyzer's context builder; the statement that groups rest on an incomplete or older graph. nonFunctional.performance: Reading one file's entities costs in proportion to that file's rows, and one repository's in proportion to that repository's rows. A file commit is one write transaction whose size is bounded by one file. A first full index holds more pending rows than today until the cross-file pass runs, and that pass does more work; this is accepted under the accuracy rule. Index jobs take precedence in the queue and a derived pass yields between its units of work, so a commit waits for at most one unit of a pass. Model calls are serial; the mid-tier pass sends only new or changed documents. Vector writes keep the plain insert for entities first stored in the same commit, so a first full index writes vectors at today's cost; the upsert, which costs more against a large vector table, is used only for changed entities and for the backfill, and Story s2's design measures it on this repository.
nonFunctional.security: No store is opened outside the daemon and no model is reached except through the local provider or the CLI providers. The ignore-file proposal sends the model file names and manifest names, not file contents, and writes into the user's repository only when no root ignore file exists. Document text sent to the mid-tier model goes through the user's own CLI session, as other mid-tier calls do.
nonFunctional.observability: Repository status carries the completeness counts and the reason a repository is incomplete. A relationship the store refuses is logged at warn with its reason and counted, not logged at debug. A fallback ignore file, a skipped language reader, a store failure after its locks were taken away, and a model-proposed capability that is off each state their cause where status is read. Each derived row carries the generation it was computed from.
nonFunctional.durability: The file commit is atomic in LMDB: after a crash a file holds its old rows or its new rows. Vectors are written after the commit and may be missing after a crash; the gap is recorded by an empty embedding marker, checked against the vector table on open, and backfilled, and the repository reads as incomplete until it is, unless the embedding backend is unavailable, which is reported as its own reason. The IndexState fields that the tables can answer are recounted when the store is opened; the rest, including the paths of files that could not be committed, are persisted in the state row and survive a restart. Every new table and value arrives by a migration step applied on open; no existing key or kind byte changes, so an older store is brought forward without a re-index. Derived tables can be dropped and recomputed without loss.

returns.meaning: as today, plus REFERENCES relations read deterministically, outside fenced and indented code blocks, in two forms. (1) Path references, with two resolution rules. (1a) Link destinations -- of an inline link or a reference-style link definition, whatever their shape -- follow Markdown's own rule: relative to the citing document's directory, or to the repository root when they start with /. In docs/a.md: 'b.md' -> docs/b.md, 'docs/b.md' -> docs/docs/b.md, '/docs/b.md' -> docs/b.md, '../src/y.ts' -> src/y.ts. (1b) Path mentions -- a backticked or bare token in running text containing a slash -- are written the way this repository's documents write paths: relative to the repository root ('src/db/relations.ts' -> src/db/relations.ts from any document), except a token starting ./ or ../, which is relative to the document's directory. A result outside the repository is not read. to = makeEntityId(repo, targetFile, 'file', targetFile). (2) Name references -- a backticked or bare token with no slash that is a file name with an extension a parser handles (e.g. 'README.md', `queue.ts`): the parser emits it as a PENDING relation with meta { docLink: true, nameRef: <the name>, class: 'no-candidate', reason: 'doc-name-ref' } and no awaitsId and no target id; it is resolved at read, never at commit (see documentRelations). In both forms the name must be one a parser handles (getParser / basenameParser.handles -- a pure name check), trailing punctuation (.,;:)!?) and a #anchor are stripped, URLs with a scheme and mailto are not read, and each distinct (containing entity, target) pair is emitted once with evidence 'extracted'; path references carry meta { awaitsId: true, docLink: true } and no meta.targetFile, so classifyFileTargets (src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts), which only classes rows carrying targetFile, never re-classes it

preconditions: markdown only; other artifact languages unchanged
links inside fenced code blocks, URLs with a scheme, mailto and pure #anchor links are not read; a #anchor suffix is dropped and the target is the file
postconditions: no file system or model access in the parser

the relation's source is the retained section whose line range holds the link, or the whole-file document when the file has no sections; a link on any line outside every retained section -- the preamble before the first heading, or a skipped tiny section -- is attributed to the file entity, so every link has a source

api.name: commitFile

parameters.name: commit
parameters.purpose: the document's entities and relations, now including its REFERENCES writes with target { stored: makeEntityId(repo, targetFile, 'file', targetFile) } and evidence 'extracted'

preconditions: before the commit, the indexer checks each document REFERENCES target id against the store (entityU64ForId, a store read with no file system access): a stored target is written as { stored: id }; an absent one as { pending: { to: id, meta: { file: <the citing document's absolute path>, repo: <the registered repository root>, awaitsId: true, docLink: true, class: 'no-candidate', reason: 'doc-link-target-absent' } } } -- file and repo are set at the indexer boundary because upsertUnresolvedRelationsInTxn (src/db/relations.ts) refuses a pending row without them as 'pending-without-file' (unwritable); the resolver does not add file for this path. 'no-candidate' is not a completeness cause, so a link to a missing, excluded or unselected file never keeps the repository incomplete; no stat or selectFile probe is made, so no probe exception can stop the document's commit

name references are NOT resolved at commit -- the commit order of a full index (one file after another, after deleting the repository's rows) would make any commit-time answer depend on which files happen to be stored yet. They are stored as pending rows (with meta.file and meta.repo, class 'no-candidate', so they never affect completeness) and resolved at read by documentRelations against the file population at that moment. The cross-file pass leaves them alone: REFERENCES is a Pass 2 kind (PASS2_KINDS in src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts), so Pass 2 and the SQL re-check (recheckSqlReferences / sqlReferencesForSettle) skip any row with meta.docLink -- a guard added there for s10's own rows
postconditions: recovery when the target appears: the target's commit is followed by the settle, whose Pass 0 (runPass0 in src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts) promotes every pending row awaiting an entity of the committed files whatever its class, carrying the row's 'extracted' evidence; in a full index, Pass 0's repository mode promotes every awaitsId row whose target is now stored. So a target created, or newly included, later regains its incoming links without the citing document being re-read
re-committing the document replaces its REFERENCES and its pending rows (sc2)

when a target file is removed, sc2 returns its incoming REFERENCES to pending (returnEdgeToPendingInTxn, which for REFERENCES first tries the SQL by-name rows; sqlByNameRows applies only between SQL entities, so a document's link falls back to the plain awaiting row); the indexer then re-reads each markdown document holding such a row (found by the s1 lookup of pending rows by awaited id) so it is re-written as 'no-candidate' and the repository returns to complete

api.name: resolveRoleProvider
api.signature: resolveRoleProvider(role: 'indexer.docRelations', cfg: AnalyzeConfig, legacyFallback?: () => LLMProvider, execution?: ConnectionExecutionContext): LLMProvider

parameters.name: legacyFallback
parameters.purpose: a builder strictly from tiers.mid, used on the indexing worker where no routing context is set

returns.meaning: the mid-tier provider; the pass refuses one whose family is not a CLI family (ac4, k3)

errors.condition: an Ollama-hosted mid tier names a model it does not declare; a provider failure

errors.type: provider failure (any error thrown by the provider call)
errors.condition: classification rule: every error thrown by provider.completeStructured, whatever its shape -- CliExitError, CliStallError, ModelCallFailedError, a spawn error (ENOENT/EACCES), the plain Error runCodex raises for an error / turn.failed event, the Error from a Claude is_error envelope, the plain Error withStructuredRetry throws with the original failure as cause (Vibe) -- is a PROVIDER failure: the pass stops, the extraction state becomes 'unavailable' with the message chain (err.message plus each cause's message), and the scheduler retries. Validation of a value the provider DID return has two disjoint cases: the value as a whole does not match the proposal schema (not an object with a proposals array of { from, to, rationale } strings) -> DocRelationsOutputInvalid, a per-document failure (the row is not rewritten, the document is retried); the value matches but an individual proposal names a source that is not an entity of the document or a target that is not stored -> only that proposal is dropped and counted (unresolvedProposals) and the row is published with the remaining proposals

postconditions: resolved on each pass, so a tier change applies without restart

the pass does not rely on resolution throwing, and it enforces the mid tier in both paths without changing the router's precedence: it first computes the effective assignment with the pure resolveRole('indexer.docRelations', cfg, repoPath) (src/analyze/context/role-router.ts), which applies the per-repo and global roleTiers precedence, and requires resolution.tier === 'mid' -- an override to another tier is refused, never followed; then, under a routing context, it takes the router's ResolvedProvider and checks its resolution is the same mid assignment; outside one (the summary worker, src/daemon/threads/summary-worker.ts) it builds from that resolution's runner and model (the mid tier's), not from an unchecked record. In both it then requires a family with a CLI kind in the model registry and a model the registry lists for that family. Any refusal records the extraction state 'unavailable' with the reason (e.g. 'indexer.docRelations is assigned to tier cheap; this capability runs only on the mid tier') and makes no call. The validated model id is the modelId stamped on rows and quality figures

api.name: completenessOf

returns.meaning: unchanged: the document-relations line is NOT a completeness reason, so a repository without proposals still reads complete (ac6)

postconditions: the docRelations status has two independent parts, persisted in the repository's doc_relation_quality row: switch ('on' | 'off' | 'not-measured', derived at read from the figures and the current validated model -- it alone decides whether eligible proposals are read) and extraction ({ state: 'ok' | 'unavailable', reason, examined, failed, computedAtGeneration?, updatedAt }, written by the pass on the summary worker in the transaction that publishes its rows, or on its own when it makes no call). Precedence: an 'unavailable' extraction never hides proposals that are on and eligible -- they were measured and still match their document's text -- it means new or changed documents are not examined; it is reported beside the switch (e.g. 'on; new documents not examined: <cause>'). api.name: docRelations.measure (daemon request)
api.signature: (params: { repoPath: string }) => Promise<{ queued: true; setHash: string; checked: number }>

returns.type: { queued: true; setHash: string; checked: number }
returns.meaning: the set was valid and a doc-relations-measure job is queued on the summary lane; the figures appear in repo.stats docRelations when it finishes

errors.condition: the set file is missing or fails its schema check; a link appears twice; one link carries both real:true and real:false; or it holds fewer than 100 distinct IMPLIED real links (real links that are not already extracted links of their document); the response names which

preconditions: registered in buildHandlerRuntime (src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts) and classified ['docRelations.measure', 'indexing', false] in src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts, so it runs on the queue-owning indexing thread
postconditions: the set is exhaustive for each document it lists: every real link of a listed document is in it (real:false entries are optional, recorded negatives)

link identity is canonical: (from = repository-relative document path, to = repository-relative file path, or path#symbol for a code symbol), paths normalised (no ./ or ..; #anchors on documents dropped)

the job runs the model over every listed document with the current validated mid-tier model, one at a time on the summary lane, and measures exactly the population readers admit: each proposal is normalised to the same identity (from -> the document's path, to -> the target file entity's path or the symbol's file#name), duplicates collapse, and proposals that duplicate an extracted link of the document are removed, as the pass removes them before storing

the set's real links are split into extracted (also read from the text) and implied (all others); precision = |admitted and real| / |admitted|, where an admitted pair absent from the set counts as wrong since the set is exhaustive; recall = |admitted and implied| / |implied|; the switch needs >= 100 implied links, precision >= 0.95 and recall >= 0.60. Example: 100 proposals duplicating extracted links plus 5 wrong ones admit 5 proposals, precision 0/5 -> off. The extracted-link recovery (|extracted read| / |extracted in set|) is recorded beside the figures for information and does not switch anything. One doc_relation_quality row is written; no proposal rows are written

validation happens before queuing; a provider failure during the job writes no new measurement figures (existing figures are kept unchanged) and, in one transaction, creates the repository's doc_relation_quality row if it does not exist and sets its extraction to { state: 'unavailable', reason: <the message chain>, updatedAt }, so repo.stats and the status board read the cause

api.name: documentRelations
api.signature: documentRelations(entityId: string, direction: 'out' | 'in'): Promise<{ readonly rows: readonly { readonly from: string; readonly to: string; readonly kind: 'REFERENCES'; readonly evidence: RelationEvidence; readonly computedAtGeneration?: number }[]; readonly generation: number; readonly staleProposals: number }>

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.purpose: a document, section, file or code entity

parameters.name: direction
parameters.purpose: relationships the entity makes, or that point at it

returns.meaning: rows: the stored REFERENCES rows touching the entity, then the entity's name references resolved now (outgoing: each pending doc-name-ref row of the entity whose name matches exactly one 'file' entity of the repository through the name index, returned with evidence 'extracted'; none or several -> not returned; incoming, for a file entity: the pending doc-name-ref rows whose nameRef equals its name, kept only when it is the only file of that name), so a target indexed later, or a second file of the same name, changes the answer at once without any re-read (outNeighbors / inNeighbors with kindFilter REFERENCES and withEvidence, src/db/graph/edges.ts), then, only while the switch is on, its eligible proposals with evidence 'model' and the computedAtGeneration of the row they came from; generation: the repository's current IndexState generation; staleProposals: how many returned proposals were computed at an older generation. Eligibility (hash, model, live endpoints) keeps the hash-based cache reuse; staleness is disclosed, not filtered

preconditions: a proposal row is eligible only when: its contentHash equals the document's current file-entity hash; its modelId equals the current mid-tier model; and each proposal's from and to entities are stored now. Ineligible rows and proposals are skipped at read and pruned by the next pass without a model call when only an endpoint vanished

store read policy: the new handles docRelationProposals and docRelationQuality are added to structuralTables in src/db/graph/store.ts, so session-memory analyzer executions may read them (guardGraphHandles denies reads only for handles outside that set) while every mutator stays denied (graphMutators) -- the same policy as subsystem and subsystemByFile
postconditions: consumers: the doc.mention exploration (src/analyze/explore/doc-mention.ts) adds, AT READ, to each DocMentionHit (src/analyze/explore/types.ts) a 'related' list of { entityId, file, evidence, computedAtGeneration? }, its answer states the origin with evidenceOrigin(evidence, { one: 'related document link', many: 'related document links' }) (ac3), and when staleProposals > 0 it adds the line 'N model-proposed links were computed from an older index (generation G; the index is now at generation C)' as the HLD requires of a reader that finds an older generation; and a new session-class daemon request search.doc_relations { entityId, direction } (registered in handler-runtime.ts, classified 'session' in method-class.ts) whose handler first calls await guardSearchRequest({ entityIds: [entityId] }) (src/daemon/search-guard.ts) exactly as search.callers and search.callees do, so a request about a repository being indexed, or whose index did not finish, is refused with the named error and progress figures; otherwise it returns the same { rows, generation, staleProposals }

unchanged by design: findCallers / findCallees stay CALLS-only; outNeighbors / inNeighbors, the closure traversal (src/db/graph/traversal.ts) and graph_query return stored rows only -- proposals never enter multi-hop traversal, because those reads return entities without evidence and a proposal there could not be marked as proposed by a model

cache: the 'related' lists are never cached. doc.mention is cacheable and the executor serves a cache hit without running the runner (src/analyze/explore/executor.ts: executePlanWithContext and stepPlanWithContext, and the third hit path), and the exploration-cache key (src/db/exploration-cache.ts: repoId, lastIndexedAt, param hash) carries no proposal, quality, set or model revision. So the runner's output is stored WITHOUT 'related' and without the staleness line, and a single function attachDocRelations(output) is applied to every doc.mention output after it is obtained -- fresh or from any of the executor's hit paths -- computing 'related' and the staleness line from documentRelations at that moment. A measurement that switches proposals off, a new proposal row, a model or role change, or a set change therefore takes effect on the next read, with no cache invalidation. Rows already in the cache have the stored shape unchanged (no 'related'), so they need no version bump and are served with 'related' attached. Two further paths serve doc.mention outputs without the runner and are covered too: (a) stepPlanWithContext restores earlier outputs from resumeState into outputsById and results and skips them ('if (outputsById.has(originalExp.id)) continue'); attachDocRelations is applied to every restored doc.mention output, in both maps, when a paused run resumes (src/analyze/explore/executor.ts, src/analyze/session-reuse.ts); (b) a synthesized context bundle cached by buildShaperBundle (src/analyze/context/driver.ts, src/analyze/context/cache.ts) is fresh only while the repository's docRelationsRevision equals the one stamped in its meta, beside the existing isStaleByIndexer check; docRelationsRevision(repo) is a hash of the repository's IndexState generation (advanced by every file commit, so an endpoint removed, a second file of the same name, or any file event changes it -- lastIndexedAt alone does not move on a file event), the quality row (figures and their updatedAt), the latest proposal-publication stamp, the current validated mid-tier model id and the current set hash. It is captured once, when the bundle's inputs are gathered, stamped into the bundle's meta, and compared through the shared cache front door (the same place servedFromCache / isStaleByIndexer decide reuse in src/analyze/context/driver.ts), for every bundle whose explorations include doc.mention; a bundle without document relations keeps today's rule. A measurement, a publication, a model or role change, a set change or any commit therefore makes such a cached bundle stale before attachDocRelations could be skipped

dataModelChanges.entity: REFERENCES relationship from a document section (extracted)
dataModelChanges.details: Endpoints: from a 'section' or 'document' entity, or the 'file' entity for a link in a skipped tiny section, of a markdown file; to the 'file' entity of the target file (a document or a code file), named by a path (link destination, including a sibling name, or a token with a slash). A reference by bare file name is stored as a pending row (class 'no-candidate', reason 'doc-name-ref', meta.nameRef) and resolved at read to the only file of that name, if there is exactly one. Direction: the citing document -> the cited file. Cardinality: a source entity has zero or more; a target file is cited by zero or more; at most one row per (source entity, target file). Ownership: the source document's file commit, as a stored row when the target is stored and otherwise as a pending row { awaitsId, docLink, class 'no-candidate', reason 'doc-link-target-absent' } that Pass 0 promotes when the target commits; replaced wholesale when it is re-read. Evidence 'extracted' (sc3). Compatibility: uses the existing REFERENCES kind byte; no key or kind byte changes; existing stores gain rows only when a document is next read (a full reindex fills them). Current invariant it might break: today no REFERENCES row leaves a document, so any reader that follows out-edges of document entities (outNeighbors without kindFilter, closure) now meets them; callers/callees are unaffected (CALLS-only).

Key: repoId(u32) ++ document file path (repository-relative). Value: { contentHash: the document's file-entity hash when examined, modelId, computedAtGeneration (DerivedStamp, sc1), proposals: [{ from, to, rationale <= 200 chars }] }. One row per document the pass examined. Lifetime, following the HLD (the added tables are cleared with the repository's rows): deleteEntitiesForRepo clears the repository's rows; when it is called with carryDocSummaries (the full index and repo.reindex, src/indexer/index.ts), the same transaction copies them to a carry area, exactly as carryDocSummariesInTxn does for summaries (src/db/doc-summaries.ts), so no row is readable during the rebuild; after the rebuild a restore step, beside restoreCarriedDocSummaries and before the doc-relations pass is requested, writes back each carried row whose document's current file-entity hash equals its contentHash and drops the rest. So the pass re-sends only documents whose hash or model differs (ac5). removeRepo deletes the rows and the carry area. The pass deletes a row whose document no longer exists and prunes proposals whose endpoints vanished without a model call. A failed re-examination leaves the earlier row in place but ineligible (hash differs). Proposals that duplicate an extracted REFERENCES are not stored. Added by migration step 9 (SCHEMA_VERSION 8 -> 9), which also creates the carry area; derived, so it can be dropped and recomputed.

Key: repoId. Value: { figures?: QualityFigures { checked (distinct implied real links), proposed, right, found, precision, recall, extractedRecovery, modelId, measuredAt, setHash }, extraction: { state: 'ok' | 'unavailable', reason, examined, failed, computedAtGeneration?, updatedAt } }. figures are written only by a successful measurement job; extraction by the doc-relations pass and by the measurement job's failure path (which keeps the figures and creates the row if absent). The switch is derived at read: 'on' iff figures exist with checked >= 100, precision >= 0.95, recall >= 0.60, modelId equal to the current validated mid-tier model and setHash equal to the current set; 'off' with figures otherwise; 'not-measured' without figures. The extraction state never changes the switch (see completenessOf). Read by repo.stats and the status board.

.insrc/doc-relations-checked.json: { links: [{ from: repository-relative document path, to: repository-relative file path or path#symbol, real: boolean }] }. Exhaustive for each listed document. Identity is the normalised (from, to) pair; a duplicate pair or a pair labelled both ways is rejected. At least 100 DISTINCT real:true pairs are required. Built by the user (or drafted by a subagent and then hand-checked by the user) -- open question.
{ id: 'indexer.docRelations', criticality: 'peripheral', defaultTier: 'mid' } appended to the role taxonomy.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: The doc-relations job is queued only when IndexState.graphComplete, through a scheduler shaped like the subsystem scheduler (pacing on actual start, retry with back-off); every proposal row carries computedAtGeneration; reads do not filter proposals by generation (the content-hash cache stays reusable) but disclose it: documentRelations returns the current generation and how many proposals are older, and its consumers state it, as the HLD requires of a reader that finds an older generation; the status line reports the generation the last pass ran at. The document-relations status is a sibling field of RepoCompleteness and never a completeness reason. The two new handles join the structural read set in src/db/graph/store.ts so session-memory analyzer reads are allowed and writes stay denied.

Extracted REFERENCES are ordinary relations in the document's FileCommit, evidence 'extracted': { stored: id } when the target file entity is stored, otherwise a pending row awaiting that id with class 'no-candidate' (reason 'doc-link-target-absent'), which is not a completeness cause and which the s1 Pass 0 promotes when the target commits -- so a target created or included later regains its links without a re-read. When a target file is removed, sc2 returns the incoming REFERENCES to pending; the indexer re-reads each citing markdown document (found by the s1 lookup of pending rows by awaited id), which re-writes the link as 'no-candidate'.

Extracted rows carry 'extracted' and are read by every existing relationship read with that evidence. Proposals are never written as graph rows; they are read only through documentRelations, which appends eligible proposals with evidence 'model' while the switch is on, and through its two consumers (doc.mention hits and search.doc_relations), each of which carries the evidence into its output (ac3). Multi-hop traversal and caller/callee reads are unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: No CLI provider is available: the mid tier names a non-CLI family or no model, or a CLI family resolves but its session is not signed in
errorCases.detection: before any call: resolveRole gives an effective tier other than mid, or the family has no CLI kind / no listed model; during a pass: ANY error thrown by the provider call (CliExitError, CliStallError, ModelCallFailedError, spawn errors, the plain Errors from Codex error/turn.failed events, Claude is_error envelopes and Vibe's wrapped retry failure) -- classified as a provider failure by origin, not by shape
errorCases.response: The pass stops, persists extraction 'unavailable' with the message chain, writes no rows, and returns a non-outcome result so the scheduler counts a failed pass and retries with its back-off (re-validating each time). Proposals already on and eligible stay readable; never-measured repositories read nothing; extracted links are unaffected; the first successful call sets extraction back to 'ok'
errorCases.userImpact: Status says model-proposed document relationships are not being extracted and why (ac6); answers use extracted links, plus earlier proposals only if the switch is on and they are still eligible

errorCases.scenario: The provider returns a value that does not match the proposal schema as a whole for one document
errorCases.detection: the pass checks the returned value's shape (an object with a proposals array of { from, to, rationale } strings) and raises DocRelationsOutputInvalid; an error thrown by the provider call itself is a provider failure, and a well-formed value with individual bad proposals is the next case
errorCases.response: That document's row is not rewritten; an earlier row stays only as inactive cache (its hash no longer matches, so documentRelations skips it); the failure is counted in the outcome, the pass continues with the next document; a pass with failures re-queues with back-off
errorCases.userImpact: The document is re-examined later; nothing wrong is stored

errorCases.scenario: A well-formed value contains individual proposals whose source is not an entity of the document or whose target is not a stored entity
errorCases.detection: each proposal's target path/symbol is resolved against the store (file entity id by deterministic id; symbol by name within the named file) and its source against the document's entities
errorCases.response: Only those proposals are dropped and counted (unresolvedProposals) in the pass log; the row is published with the remaining proposals; nothing invalid is stored or pending
errorCases.userImpact: None; no invented relationship reaches a read

errorCases.scenario: A full index or a commit to the document happens while the pass is examining it
errorCases.detection: before writing a row the pass re-reads the document's current content hash and the IndexState generation guard as the subsystem pass does
errorCases.response: A row whose content hash no longer matches is not written (the next pass examines the new text); a pass superseded by a full index publishes nothing (reason 'superseded')
errorCases.userImpact: No stale proposal for changed text

errorCases.scenario: The hand-checked set is missing, malformed, or has fewer than 100 real links
errorCases.detection: the measurement request parses .insrc/doc-relations-checked.json with a schema check and counts real:true entries
errorCases.response: The request returns a named error (DocRelationsSetInvalid with the reason); no quality row is written; the capability stays off with state 'not-measured' or the previous figures
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told what the set lacks

errorCases.scenario: The measurement runs but falls below the bar
errorCases.detection: precision < 0.95 or recall < 0.60 computed over the set
errorCases.response: The quality row is written with the figures; the switch reads off; proposals are still computed and stored (so a later measurement or a better model can turn them on) but never merged into reads
errorCases.userImpact: Status shows 'off' with the measured figures (lc1)

errorCases.scenario: A store write of a proposal row fails
errorCases.response: The transaction aborts, the failure is logged at warn and counted as a failed document; the scheduler retries

errorCases.scenario: A proposal's endpoint disappears while its document is unchanged (a section heading moves, a target file or symbol is removed)
errorCases.detection: documentRelations checks each proposal's from and to entities exist at read; the pass checks the same for every stored row of an unchanged document
errorCases.response: The proposal is skipped at read and pruned from its row by the next pass without a model call
errorCases.userImpact: No relationship to a removed entity is shown

migration.stateBefore: Markdown is split into section/document entities joined to their file only by DEFINES (src/indexer/parser/artifact.ts); no document-to-document or document-to-code relationship is stored. Evidence bytes exist (src/db/graph/codec.ts) and the analyzer words 'model' evidence (src/analyze/explore/usage-example.ts), but nothing writes REFERENCES from documents. The only indexing model role is indexer.summarise on the cheap tier (src/config/role-taxonomy.ts).
migration.stateAfter: Each markdown document's commit carries REFERENCES with evidence 'extracted' to the files it links or names by path. Two derived sub-dbs exist: doc_relation_proposals (per-document mid-tier proposals stamped with generation, content hash and model) and doc_relation_quality (per-repository measured figures). Reads merge proposals as evidence 'model' only while the measured switch is on. repo.stats carries a docRelations field with state and reason.

migrationSteps.action: Add the role indexer.docRelations (peripheral, mid) to the role taxonomy; config reconcile carries existing config forward unchanged

Add migration step 9 (SCHEMA_VERSION 8 -> 9) on the existing chain that creates the empty doc_relation_proposals and doc_relation_quality sub-dbs; no existing row is read or rewritten. Not rollbackable in place: an older daemon refuses a store whose schema_version exceeds its own (LmdbStoreSchemaVersionMismatch in src/db/graph/store.ts)
Ship the link reader; existing stores gain extracted REFERENCES as each document is next committed; a repo.reindex fills every document at once (recommended once after the update, not required)

Ship the doc-relations pass and scheduler; it starts after the first complete graph and examines every document once (no rows yet), then only new or changed ones; with no hand-checked set the capability reads 'not-measured' and nothing merges into reads
Build the hand-checked set for this repository and run the measurement request; the switch turns on only if the figures meet the bar

migration.backwardCompat: No existing key, kind byte or relationship row changes; REFERENCES keeps its byte. The store's schema_version advances to 9, and an older daemon refuses to open it (LmdbStoreSchemaVersionMismatch): downgrading the daemon binary requires deleting the graph store (~/.insrc graph.lmdb) and re-indexing, as for every earlier schema step; there is no in-place downgrade. repo.stats and the status board gain an optional docRelations field; an older client ignores it (it maps fields explicitly), and this Story changes the CLI repository pane and both plugins to show it. Document entities gain outgoing REFERENCES rows (extracted only), each with its evidence; callers/callees stay CALLS-only and proposals appear only through documentRelations and its consumers.

alternativesConsidered.name: Extracted links in the commit; model proposals in their own stamped table, merged at read behind a measured switch
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The markdown reader emits REFERENCES (evidence 'extracted') for links and path mentions in the file commit; a queued mid-tier pass over new or changed documents writes proposals to its own generation-stamped table, which reads merge as evidence 'model' only while the recorded quality record says the capability is on.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reading: src/indexer/parser/artifact.ts gains a link reader. For each markdown link destination (sibling names included), reference-style link, and backticked or bare token in running text that names a repository path or an unambiguous file name, it emits a RelationWrite of kind REFERENCES from the section (or the whole-file document) that contains it to the target file's 'file' entity, whose id is deterministic (makeEntityId(repo, file, 'file', file)), so the target is { stored: id }; a target not stored becomes a pending row of class 'no-candidate' awaiting its id, completed by the s1 Pass 0 when the target commits. Anchors and URLs outside the repository are not read. Evidence is 'extracted' and the write goes through the ordinary file commit (sc2), so no model call happens (ac1). Model pass: a new peripheral role 'indexer.docRelations' with defaultTier 'mid' in role-taxonomy; a 'doc-relations' job on the document-summary lane, queued like the subsystem pass only when IndexState.graphComplete, which visits the documents whose content hash or model id differs from the stored row (ac5) one at a time through the mid-tier CLI provider (ac4), and writes its own table (repoId++file -> { contentHash, modelId, computedAtGeneration, proposals: [{ from, to, rationale }] }) with a migration step. Quality: a hand-checked set stored in the repository (.insrc/doc-relations-checked.json, at least 100 links), a daemon request that runs the pass over the set's documents and records { checked, proposed, right, found, precision, recall, measuredAt, modelId } in a quality row; the capability is on only when checked >= 100, precision >= 0.95 and recall >= 0.60 for the model in use, otherwise it stays off and the figures stay recorded (ac2, lc1). Reads: proposals are read only through documentRelations, which appends eligible proposals with evidence 'model' while the switch is on, and its two consumers (doc.mention hits and search.doc_relations); caller/callee reads, outNeighbors/inNeighbors, closure traversal and graph_query are unchanged and never carry proposals (ac3). Status: completeness/status carries a document-relations line: on, off with the figures, not measured, or not extracted because no CLI provider resolves for the mid tier, while indexing completes (ac6, lc2).

Extracted links are high precision: only explicit links and real repository paths, never prose guesses

A measurement request and a hand-checked set must be built and maintained; until then the model part is off

erDefinition.narrative: What s10 stores: extracted REFERENCES rows in the graph from a document's sections (or its whole-file document or file entity) to cited files, many on both ends, and two derived tables beside the graph -- per-document model proposals and a per-repository quality record that switches the proposals on.

DocumentSource.description: The citing entity of a markdown file (existing): a section, the whole-file document when the file has no headings, or the file entity for a link in a skipped tiny section.

references.description: the REFERENCES rows it makes; zero or more

CitedFile.description: The 'file' entity of a file a link names (existing; a document or a code file the full index selects).

citedBy.description: REFERENCES rows that point at it; zero or more

ExtractedReference.description: One REFERENCES graph row with evidence 'extracted', owned by the source document's file commit; at most one per (source, target file).

DocRelationRow.description: One row per examined document in doc_relation_proposals; cleared with the repository's rows on a full index and carried back only for documents whose hash is unchanged; rewritten when its content hash or the mid-tier model changes.

contentHash.description: the document's file-entity hash when examined

Proposal.description: A model-proposed REFERENCES, read as evidence 'model' only while the switch is on and the row and its endpoints are eligible.

fromId.description: id of a DocumentSource of the document

toId.description: id of a stored file or code-symbol entity

QualityFigures.description: The measured figures in a repository's doc_relation_quality row; absent until the first measurement. Decides the switch.

checked.description: distinct IMPLIED real links in the hand-checked set (real links not already extracted)

precision.description: |admitted and real| / |admitted|, admitted = proposals after removing those that duplicate extracted links

extractedRecovery.description: |extracted links read| / |extracted links in the set|, recorded for information; switches nothing

setHash.description: hash of the hand-checked set measured

DocRelationQualityRow.description: One per repository (key repoId): the optional figures and the extraction status.

ExtractionStatus.description: Written by the doc-relations pass; read by repo.stats and the status board beside the derived switch.

examined.description: documents examined by the last pass

computedAtGeneration.description: generation the last pass ran at
